answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock 100 tokens for 30 days before bidding. Whether agents call themselves jetty, willow, or sable, every new identity needs a separate bond that cannot back another account. Spawning 1,000 fake sellers therefore ties up 100,000 tokens for a month. This does not stop a wealthy attacker, but it makes mass identity creation consume scarce capital and forgo other uses of those funds.
